turns.replyText:
Can you explain the main options in simple terms?

Absolutely! Here are the main types in plain English:



Roller blinds: one flat piece of fabric that rolls up and down. Simple, affordable, and huge choice of colours.


Vertical blinds: slats that hang down and can tilt or pull to the side. Great for big windows and patio doors.


Venetian blinds: horizontal slats (usually wood, faux wood, or aluminium) that tilt to fine-tune light. Classic and smart looking.


Roman blinds: fabric that folds into soft pleats when raised. Very cosy and stylish, ideal for living rooms and bedrooms.


Pleated blinds: thin folded fabric, light and tidy. Popular for conservatories and odd-shaped windows.


Day & Night (Twist) blinds: two layers of striped fabric you slide to switch between sheer and opaque. Modern and versatile.


Electric blinds: any style with a motor, so you can raise and lower them with a remote or app.

For a first-timer like me, what's the safest, easiest choice?
6:37 AM

For a first-timer, I'd say roller blinds are the easiest win!

They're simple to measure for, simple to fit, and there are no fiddly slats or cords to worry about. You just choose a fabric, and they work well in pretty much any room. If you want extra peace of mind on fitting, our no-drill options like Twist2Go or Click2Go just clip straight onto the window frame, no screws or tools needed.

A couple of quick tips as a beginner:



Measure at the top of the recess in three places (left, middle, right) and use the smallest measurement.


Choose "recess size" when ordering and we'll make the small deductions for you, so the blind fits perfectly.



Please note: Twist2Go and Click2Go No Drill blinds are only suitable for recess fitting and cannot be fitted outside the recess. If you're ordering one of these, measure at the top of the recess where the blind will be fitted, and we'll make the necessary deductions.
